messages:
sara_support: Heads-up — multiple customer requests (acct acme-corp) are being routed to us-west instead of eu-central and failing auth. They report 502s on inference calls and 600-900ms p50 latency. curl shows X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2. Anyone confirming header rewrite after last gateway deploy?

derek_infra: on it. Which endpoints? examples?

sara_support: POST /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Example curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer redacted' -H 'X-Region-Preference: eu-central-1' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers: `X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2`, `x-envoy-original-dst: 100.64.1.23:443`

matthias_oncall: oncall-bot created INC-2026-042. Seeing routing metrics spike for eu-central->us-west failovers. Possible L7 header rewrite bug from the gateway canary last night (derek?)

derek_infra: I rolled out gateway canary at 1777650000. Config change: added `route_metadata: prefer_local_by_header` + lua filter to copy `X-Region-Preference` to `x-redwood-preferred-region`. Investigating if header case/whitelist missed.

alisa_engineer: quick check — envoys drop headers with underscores by default. Are we using `x_redwood_preferred_region` anywhere? Also Envoy has `preserve_external_request_id` toggles. Could be case-sensitivity.

sara_support: customer says token validation fails when requests land in us-west because their key is tied to eu VPC. So auth error 401 from internal auth-service, not from client.

derek_infra: I see an ACL in gateway vhost that rewrites `X-Redwood-Region` on the response using `%RESPONSE_REGION%` var. If the incoming header was copied to `x-redwood-preferred-region` but response rewrite only looks for `X-Region-Preference`, mismatch.

derek_infra: reproducing with curl on staging:
```
$ curl -v -H 'X-Region-Preference: eu-central-1' https://staging-gw.internal/generate
> X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2
> x-redwood-preferred-region: eu-central-1
```
So the backend sees preferred region, but the gateway still sets X-Redwood-Region based on upstream cluster selection (wrong cluster chosen)

matthias_oncall: routing decision seems prior to lua filter execution. Suggest adding debug logs to the decision path or temporarily revert canary. Are there connections cached to us-west shards?

alisa_engineer: Also check the traffic-split policy that uses `region_affinity` cookie. There was an optimization that treats empty cookie as `prefer_local`. If header present but both cookie and header used, precedence bug might prefer cookie.

sara_support: Customer provided request-id 01F7KX2. Can we map it in logs?

derek_infra: Found it in access logs -> routed to us-west cluster because `cookie.region=us-west` on their client IP. Cookie TTL is 30d. But why did cookie exist? It was set by our legacy L7 fallback for legacy endpoints.

matthias_oncall: Plan: 1) patch canary to respect header precedence over cookie (hotfix), 2) backfill script to clear stale cookies for active customers, 3) rollback if hotfix causes regression. Any objections? :thumbsup:

alisa_engineer: +1. I'll prepare patch and unit tests. Also adding integration test to simulate header vs cookie precedence.

sara_support: Communicated to customer: temporary workaround — include `Cookie: region=eu-central` to force routing. They can also set region param in request body.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 opened by matthias_oncall. Priority P2. Slack channel #inc-2026-042 created.

derek_infra: I'll deploy hotfix to canary in 10m and monitor. If latency spikes, will rollback.

sara_support: Thanks — please post updates here and tag me when resolved. Customer is waiting and has billing impact.

matthias_oncall: update 10:15 UTC: hotfix deployed to canary, routed test request to eu-central properly. Monitoring shows decreased cross-region egress. Keeping open until full rollout.
